simple.meaning: זֵכֶר (zêker) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “a memento , abstractly recollection (rarely if ever); by implication, commemoration.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 23 times across Exodus, Deuteronomy, Esther, Job, Psalms, and 4 more, beginning at Exodus 3:15. Its contexts include family, city, land, Israel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to זֵכֶר (H2143).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.

definitions.short: a memento , abstractly recollection (rarely if ever); by implication, commemoration
definitions.full: H2143. zeker II. זֶ֫כֶר noun masculine Exod 17:14 , see following. זֵ֫כֶר noun masculine Psa 9:7 remembrance, memorial (compare Hpt Hebraica. 1885, 230 ) — ׳ז absolute 111:4 ; construct Deut 25:19 +; זֶכֶר construct Exod 17:14 van d. H; suffix זִכְרִי 3:15 , זִכְרְךָ Isa 26:8 +, זִכְרֶ֑ךָ Psa 6:6 , זִכְרוֺ Hosea 12:6 +, זִכְרָם Deut 32:26 +: — 1 remembrance, memory: a. of persons or people, blotted out by their destruction , Exod 17:14 (E; with מחה ) = Deut 25:19 ; 32:26 ( השׁבית ) Psa 34:17 ; 109:15 (both הכרית ), 9:7 ( אבד ), Job 18:17 ( אבד ; || שֵׁם ), Isa 26:14 ( אבּד ); compare on other hand ׳ז עוֺלָם as portion of righteous. b. of ׳י Psa 6:6 ; 102:13 (|| אַתָּה = יהוה ). c. of ׳י s character and works Psa 30:5 ; 97:12 ; 111:4 . d. remembrance of particular days, i.e. their observance Est 9:28 ( יְמֵי הַמּוּרִים ). 2 memorial , by which one is remembered: a. nearly = ׳ז לִבְרָכָה צַדִּיק שֵׁם, Prov 10:7 (|| שֵׁם ), compare also Eccl 9:5 (with נשׁכח ); especially of ׳י Exod 3:15 (E), Hosea 12:6 ; Isa 26:8 ; Psa 135:13 (all || שֵׁם ). b. = renown (of Israel) Hosea 14:8 (compare VB).

occurrences.englishText: God said moreover to Moses, “You shall tell the children of Israel this, ‘Yahweh, the God of your fathers, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob, has sent me to you.’ This is my name forever, and this is my memorial to all generations.
Yahweh said to Moses, “Write this for a memorial in a book, and rehearse it in the ears of Joshua: that I will utterly blot out the memory of Amalek from under the sky.”

Therefore it shall be, when Yahweh your God has given you rest from all your enemies all around, in the land which Yahweh your God gives you for an inheritance to possess it, that you shall blot out the memory of Amalek from under the sky. You shall not forget.
I said that I would scatter them afar.

and that these days should be remembered and kept throughout every generation, every family, every province, and every city; and that these days of Purim should not fail from among the Jews, nor their memory perish from their offspring,† or, seed
His memory will perish from the earth.
I am weary with my groaning.
But Yahweh reigns forever.
For his anger is but for a moment.
The righteous cry, and Yahweh hears,
Be glad in Yahweh, you righteous people!
You will arise and have mercy on Zion;
Let them be before Yahweh continually,
He has caused his wonderful works to be remembered.
For he will never be shaken.
Your name, Yahweh, endures forever;
They will utter the memory of your great goodness,
The memory of the righteous is blessed,
For the living know that they will die, but the dead don’t know anything, neither do they have any more a reward; for their memory is forgotten.
Yes, in the way of your judgments, Yahweh, we have waited for you.
The dead shall not live.
Therefore turn to your God.
Ephraim, what have I to do any more with idols?
